pull.title: 🛡️ Sentinel: Fix IPv6 literal bracket resolution in download pinning
pull.body:
🛡️ Sentinel Security Fix: Strip brackets from IPv6 literal hostnames in `resolvePinnedAddress`

- 💡 **Vulnerability/Issue**: Node's WHATWG `URL.hostname` preserves surrounding square brackets for IPv6 address literals (e.g. `[2606:4700:4700::1111]`). Passing bracketed IPv6 hostnames to `dns.lookup` in `resolvePinnedAddress` causes DNS lookup failures (`ENOTFOUND`), preventing legitimate public IPv6 external downloads from functioning and causing unhandled resolution failures during SSRF pinning.
- 🎯 **Impact**: Public IPv6 literal download requests fail erroneously before DNS pinning and SSRF validation can complete.
- 🔧 **Fix**: Strip surrounding brackets with `.replace(/^\[|\]$/g, '')` in `resolvePinnedAddress` before calling `lookup(...)`.
- ✅ **Verification**: Added unit test in `src/download.test.ts` verifying that bracketed IPv6 literals are stripped when passed to `lookup(...)` and that connection parameters match. Ran `npm run test:run`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, and `npm run build` with all checks passing.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [7678477791282394596](https://jules.google.com/task/7678477791282394596) started by @dorogoy*

commit.message:
fix: strip brackets from IPv6 host in resolvePinnedAddress

WHATWG URL.hostname retains enclosing brackets for IPv6 literals
(e.g., [2001:db8::1]). Node dns.lookup fails with ENOTFOUND on bracketed
IPv6 literals. Strip surrounding brackets in resolvePinnedAddress before
calling lookup.
